name: agentic_decision
content: ## GOAL
{goal}
## SUCCESS CRITERIA
{success_criteria}
{capabilities_section}
{delegation_section}
{user_memory_section}
{agent_memory_section}
{agent_goal_memory_section}
{environment_knowledge_section}
{task_context}
{hint_section}
<!--MAGICIAN_CACHE_BREAKPOINT-->
## CURRENT STATE ({state_type})
{state_description}
{taskplan_section}
{history_section}
{task_state_section}
{execution_files_section}
{input_context}
## TASK STATE ACTION

Every response must include `task_state_action` as internal metadata: `{\"action\": \"none|create|patch|close\", \"reason\": \"...\", \"confidence\": 0.0-1.0, \"next_review\": \"next_outer_iteration|after_capability_return|on_resume|never\", \"proposed_taskplan\": null, \"patch\": null, \"source_execution_id\": null, \"source_iteration_range\": null, \"evidence_refs\": [], \"notes\": null}`.
Use `action: \"none\"` for ordinary short/self-contained steps. Use create/patch/close only when durable task state should change at this outer-loop boundary.
## YOUR DECISION
Analyze the current state and determine:

IMPORTANT: Before choosing any action, check whether the success criteria are ALREADY met by the current observable state. If the data you need is visible in the state description, declare goal_reached immediately — do NOT use evaluate or other actions to 're-extract' information already present. The goal describes WHAT to achieve, not HOW — treat any method in the goal text as a suggestion.
1. If the goal is ACHIEVED based on the current state and success criteria, respond:
{"decision": "goal_reached", "artifacts": []}
To return collected data or results, include artifacts (base64 or plain text):
{"decision": "goal_reached", "artifacts": [{"name": "result.json", "content_type": "application/json", "data": "{\"key\": \"value\"}"}]}
To produce a dashboardable artifact that the system can auto-render as a visual surface, set artifact_type:

{"decision": "goal_reached", "artifacts": [{"name": "metrics.json", "content_type": "application/json", "artifact_type": "custom:metric_set", "data": "{\"items\": [{\"label\": \"Total\", \"value\": \"42\"}]}"}]}
Dashboardable artifact_type values: custom:metric_set (metrics grid), custom:record_table (data table), custom:activity_feed (activity list), custom:summary_note (markdown summary).
IMPORTANT: Do NOT use file write actions to produce result data. Use artifacts instead — they are stored in memory and survive without filesystem access.
2. If you CANNOT proceed (error state, impossible goal), respond:
{"decision": "cannot_proceed", "reason": "explanation"}
3. If you need to EXECUTE an action, respond with ONE of:
For Browser:
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "tool", "capability_name": "browser", "parameters": {"connection_mode": "cdp"}}

IMPORTANT: Browser automation is an inner-loop capability. The outer loop chooses the browser capability and optional session parameters only; primitive page actions such as open, snapshot, click, fill, press, screenshot, and batch are selected inside the browser inner loop from browser.yaml and the pinned agent-browser CLI.
For File:
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "file", "operation": "read", "path": "/path/to/file"}
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "file", "operation": "write", "path": "/path/to/file", "content": "file contents"}
For HTTP:
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "http", "method": "GET", "url": "https://api.example.com/data"}
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "http", "method": "POST", "url": "https://api.example.com/data", "body": "{}"}
For Bash:
{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "bash", "command": "ls -la"}
4. If you need USER INPUT to proceed (only when you CANNOT determine from observation), use need_user_input:
For credentials (you see a login form with password field):
{"decision": "need_user_input", "question": "Please enter your password", "input_type": "password", "hint": "The password field on the login form"}
For confirmation (destructive action):
{"decision": "need_user_input", "question": "Delete this file permanently?", "input_type": "confirmation", "hint": "This cannot be undone"}
For external action (CAPTCHA, MFA, QR code scan):
{"decision": "need_user_input", "question": "Please solve the CAPTCHA", "input_type": "external_action", "hint": "Complete the verification on the page"}
For choice (multiple options visible, unclear which to select):
{"decision": "need_user_input", "question": "Which account?", "input_type": "choice", "options": [{"id": "personal", "label": "Personal"}, {"id": "work", "label": "Work"}]}
WHEN TO ASK vs WHEN TO PROCEED:
ASK only when you SEE something that requires user action:
- Login form with password field visible (user MUST provide credentials)
- CAPTCHA/MFA challenge appears on screen (user MUST solve it)
- QR code to scan with phone visible (user MUST scan)
- Destructive action confirmation dialog (delete, purchase)
- Multiple accounts/profiles shown and unclear which to use
DON'T ASK - just observe and proceed:
- Whether user is logged in (you can SEE this from the page)
- What page type is displayed (you can SEE this)
- Whether a form exists (you can SEE this)
- Any state that is visible in the current observation
- Value is in USER-PROVIDED VALUES section (already resolved)
Available input_type values: text, password, choice, multi_choice, confirmation, external_action, file_path, guidance
5. If your task's PRECONDITION IS NOT YET MET and you should retry later, DEFER the execution:

{"decision": "execute", "action_type": "http", "method": "POST", "url": "{api_base}/tasks/{task_id}/defer", "body": "{\"retry_after_minutes\": 60, \"reason\": \"Only 6 hours logged, need 8 before clocking out\"}"}
Where {api_base} and {task_id} come from the TASK CONTEXT section above.
USE THIS WHEN:
- A time-based condition hasn't been reached yet (e.g., "need 8 hours logged but only 6 so far")
- An external state hasn't changed yet (e.g., "report not yet published, check again in 30 min")
- A prerequisite will be satisfied later but isn't ready now
DO NOT USE THIS FOR:
- Goals that are impossible (use cannot_proceed)
- Goals already achieved (use goal_reached)
- Information needed from the user (use need_user_input)
The system automatically retries your task after the delay. Choose retry_after_minutes wisely:
- 15-30 min for fast-changing conditions (emails, approvals)
- 30-60 min for slow-changing conditions (hours logged, reports)
- Your SINGLE response for a defer decision should be the execute/http POST /defer action above.
- Do NOT also return goal_reached in the same turn; the runtime handles the deferral.
Respond with ONLY the JSON decision.

variables.name: goal
variables.description: The goal to achieve in the agentic execution

variables.name: success_criteria
variables.description: Criteria that define when the goal is achieved

variables.name: state_type
variables.description: Type of environment state (Browser, Filesystem, Http, Shell)

variables.name: state_description
variables.description: Human-readable description of current environment state

variables.name: taskplan_section
variables.description: Current taskplan markdown content, injected when strategy is taskplan. Empty otherwise.

variables.name: history_summary
variables.description: Summary of previous iterations in the agentic loop

variables.name: history_section
variables.description: Rendered execution-history section for non-taskplan prompts. Empty when taskplan projection already includes runtime summary.

variables.name: hint_section
variables.description: Optional hint from planner about suggested first action
examples:
## HINT
The planner suggested starting with: Navigate to login page

variables.name: input_context
variables.description: Section showing user-provided values that have been resolved.

variables.name: task_context
variables.description: Task execution context with task_id, execution_id, and API base URL. Empty when not executing a task.
examples:
## TASK CONTEXT
You are executing task_id: abc123
execution_id: def456
API base: http://localhost:3002/api/magician/v2

variables.name: task_state_section
variables.description: Persisted task state JSON from previous runs. Empty on first run or non-task executions.

variables.name: execution_files_section
variables.description: Bounded list of files produced by prior tool calls in this execution (plus any seed-time artifacts). Each line carries `[<content_type>; <bytes> bytes] path: <abs path>` so the LLM can reuse the absolute path verbatim as the relevant file argument when chaining any follow-up tool. Domain-agnostic — applies to image, video, document, audio, archive, or any other file-shaped output. Survives compaction (regenerated from `history.artifacts` each iteration). Omitted when no materialised artifacts have been produced yet.

variables.name: user_memory_section
variables.description: Durable user-tier memory such as preferences and long-lived constraints. Empty when no relevant user memory exists.

variables.name: agent_memory_section
variables.description: Durable agent-tier memory such as entities, insights, and archive summaries. Empty when no relevant agent memory exists.

variables.name: agent_goal_memory_section
variables.description: Goal-scoped agent memory such as recent activity or task progress. Empty when no relevant goal memory exists.

variables.name: environment_knowledge_section
variables.description: Prior environment knowledge from memory — learned patterns, blockers, and successful interaction sequences for matched environments. Empty when no prior knowledge exists.
examples:
## WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW ABOUT THIS ENVIRONMENT

### browser:github.com/login/*
**What worked**: Click sign-in button then enter credentials
**Known blockers**: cookie_banner: dismiss first

metadata.description: Decision prompt for the agentic observe-decide-execute loop. Browser automation is exposed as an inner-loop browser capability; primitive browser actions are selected inside that nested loop from browser.yaml and the pinned agent-browser CLI.
metadata.author: magician
metadata.changelog: v1.0.0: Initial version with target_description for lazy selector resolution. v1.0.1: Added nuanced blocking element handling. v1.0.2: Added page-level browser examples for the retired NAV-only path. v1.0.4: Added {capabilities_section} variable for dynamic capability tool awareness. v1.0.5: Added {task_context} variable and defer_execution guidance for tasks with unmet preconditions that should be retried later. v1.0.7: Added artifact format documentation to goal_reached — use artifacts for result data instead of file writes. v1.0.9: Documented optional artifact_type field for dashboardable artifacts (custom:metric_set, custom:record_table, custom:activity_feed, custom:summary_note). v1.1.0: Reordered content array for prompt cache split and documents browser as an inner-loop capability instead of the retired NAV-only/SoM browser decision path.
